chunks: Aḥmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from more than one person, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abī al-Jārūd, who said:

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام said: “What do the people resent from us? For by Allah, we are the tree of the prophethood, the House of mercy, the معدن of knowledge, and the place where the angels come and go.”

key_terms.بَيْتُ الرَّحْمَةِ: the household specially associated with divine mercy
key_terms.شَجَرَةُ النُّبُوَّةِ: the rooted source and living extension of prophethood
key_terms.مَعْدِنُ الْعِلْمِ: the mine or primary source of sacred knowledge
key_terms.مُخْتَلَفُ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the place frequented by angels, where they come and go
key_terms.يَنْقِمُ: resents, finds fault with, or harbors aversion toward

ai.seo_question: How does Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام describe the status of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the exalted spiritual and divinely granted station of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام describes them as the source of prophethood’s legacy, the abode of divine mercy, the معدن of knowledge, and the locus of angelic descent and return.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from someone else, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What makes the people resentful from us<sup>asws</sup>. We<sup>asws</sup>, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, are the tree of Prophet-hood, and the House of Mercy, and the Mine of Knowledge, and the inter-change of Angels Where Angels come and go)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ahmad ibn Mahran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from several people from Hammad ibn ’Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abdallah (a.s.) from ibn Jarud who has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) has said the following.

“What is it obscures us to people? (People do not maintain hostility towards us.) We, I swear by Allah, are the tree of the prophet-hood, the house of blessings, the mine of knowledge and the center wherein angels interchange.”
